result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` is now classified as mock-resources test code, whatever follows, at any depth and with backslash paths. The new test and the existing `SourceFileFilterTest` pass (3 and 6 tests, 0 failures).

**Change** in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`: I replaced the two mock conventions (`.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` and `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*`) with one convention:

`(.*[/\\])?(__)?mock[^/\\]*[/\\].*`

The `[^/\\]*` part lets the rest of the folder name be any character except a separator, so `mock`, `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe` and `mock模拟` all match. The match has to start at a separator or at the beginning of the path, and must end in a separator. That keeps `remock/`, `demo/` and `src/main/java/` out, and files like `mock.java` or `mockery.java` don't match because they have no folder segment after the name. The existing `mockapi`, `[Mm]ocks`, and `_mock.*` conventions are unchanged.

**New test:** `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsMockTest.java` covers the new cases, the folder names that were already test code, and the paths that must stay in main scope.

Nothing is committed.
